question.text: Mr. Shridhar Kaul's 'Deccan Infra Credit Fund' (Cat II Debt AIF) is structuring a INR 300 crore facility to finance an M&A transaction for a mid-market acquirer. The target has a 4x debt/EBITDA already. Per Chapter 9, which structural tool is typically used in such 'leveraged loan / acquisition financing' deals?

answer.text: Pure senior bank debt only — no AIF involvement possible.

Sub-ordinate debt / mezzanine layered on top of existing senior debt, sometimes using SPV structures for ring-fencing, with structured repayments pegged to cash flow or future financings; may include equity kickers.

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 9: 'Some private debt funds also finance sub-ordinate debt, in the form of leveraged loans which is used in funding companies with high amount of senior debt on their balance sheet. These structures enable special situation financings such as stressed asset resolutions, securitised debt issuances in the private credit market, promoter financing through structured credit, and LBO financing for listed companies with good track record and prime rated structured financing.' Plus 'structured repayment of the principal amounts pegged to cash flow or future financings' and 'Most sub-ordinated debt structures have equity kickers'. The Trap: Option A excludes AIFs artificially — AIFs are the natural providers of this sub-debt layer. Option C is Cat III. Option D misses the debt structure entirely. Cross-Exam Context: XV covers acquisition-financing structures. XIX-A covers concept. XIX-C all-cat covered leveraged loans. Manager's Pro-Tip: When structuring an AIF-funded leveraged loan over existing senior bank debt, get an inter-creditor agreement (ICA) signed upfront. Indian banking lobby has historically been hostile to AIF sub-debt in covenant-breach scenarios — the ICA protects your standstill rights and cure periods in a distress scenario.
